correctness.rationale: PASS: For odd-characteristic nondegenerate B and ordered Xi with all XiXj=0, skew-adjointness implies B(X_i v,X_j w)=0, so joint image U is totally isotropic and each Xi annihilates U^perp. Fixing isotropic U, Xi factors through V/U^perp≅U* and is exactly an alternating map U*→U, with q^binom(r,2) choices per Xi, and all supported products vanish automatically. Möbius inversion on the subspace lattice gives the spanning-image factor A_{r,k}(q), then the classical isotropic extension-line/flag counts yield the three Witt-type I_V(r) formulas. The rank-zero tuple is counted once, rank one impossible, n=1 and k=1 included. Independently enumerated all actual 4x4 skew-adjoint squarezero matrices over F3 and all pairwise zero-product ordered pairs, obtaining rank profile {0:1,2:64}; the source explicit n6 hyperbolic two-generator rank-three witness follows from independent block multiplication. Proof, not prime-field finite test, covers odd prime powers and all n,k.
residual_risks: Independent matrix enumeration checked q=3 n=4 k=2 only; full prime power and all n,k derive from proof.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Unrestricted mutually annihilating matrix pairs, single symmetric nilpotents, and commuting Lie pairs do not determine joint-image-rank counts for skew-adjoint zero-product k-tuples in both Witt types. Boos–Cerulli work over C on degeneration orders of self-dual quiver representations and does not tabulate such finite-field point counts. The critical isotropic-map/alternating-form calculation is elementary but the combined exact type-resolved stratum distribution was not covered in the inspected primary texts. Residual possibility of equivalent results in Hall-polynomial/alternating-pencil or self-dual quiver count literature.
